newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.

text.p: TRIAL OF GENITAL HERPES VACCINE
Volunteers are being sought in the western Sydney area to help researchers in a trial of a genital herpes vaccine.
Professor Anthony Cunningham from Westmead Hospital, says a prerequisite for participation in the trial is that one partner in a relationship has genital herpes and the other is free of infection.
Professor Cunningham says herpes is one of the most common human infections, with one in six Australians infected by the herpes simplex virus which causes genital herpes in about half those infected.
He says while drug treatments can shorten the disease period, vaccines offer the best hope for preventing infection.
Those wishing to take part in the trial should call toll free on 1800-24-23-25.
BESIEGED ABC BOSS GETS SUPPORT FROM CHAIRMAN
ABC Chairman, Donald McDonald, has come out in support of Managing Director, Brian Johns.
Mr McDonald says in a statement that the broadcaster's board is satisfied with the answers provided to questions on the Whitlam lecture raised by Senator Alston.
He says there was no external influence on the decision to air the program, and that Mr Johns is appropriately handling the flaws identified in the commissioning process.
CROC VICTIM FACES SIX-TO-EIGHT WEEKS IN HOSPITAL
The father of the north Queensland animal handler crushed by a crocodile at a tourist attraction last Friday says she appears to be recovering well.
Twenty-two year old Karla Bredl is in a stable condition in Mackay Base Hospital's intensive care unit with a broken thigh and pelvic injuries.
Ms Bredl was bitten by a four metre crocodile after slipping while feeding it at the Whitsunday Wildlife Park.
Doctors say it could be six to eight weeks before she's released.
Her father, Joe Bredl, says she hasn't said much about her ordeal, but did say she remembered what had happened when he asked her.
WILLIAMS SAYS MONEY SHOULD BE THERE FOR RETRIAL
The Federal Attorney-General, Daryl Williams, says New South Wales should have enough money to provide legal aid for the retrial of a man on serious drugs charges.
The New South Wales legal Aid Commission says it's not policy to provide funding for second trials, such as that of Yves Marini, charged under Commonwealth law with possessing cocaine.
But Mr Williams says New South Wales has been fully funded to provide legal aid for Commonwealth matters this financial year.
Mr Williams says legal Aid Commissions have been using Commonwealth money for cases arising under state law, and that's why New South Wales lacks money for the Marini case.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
